        private static ComputedContentProfileResult ComputeAndPublishActualContentProfile()
        {
            long capturedGen = -1;
            try
            {
                _globalCache.ClearComputationError();
                var snapshot = _globalCache.CaptureStateSnapshot();
                capturedGen = snapshot.generation;
                if (snapshot.policy == null)
                {
                    throw new InvalidOperationException("ContentProfile computation requires an explicit expected package policy to be configured before trusted actual content profile success. Status: UNCONFIGURED (BLOCKED_NO_POLICY).");
                }

                var manifest = CollectActualContentProfileManifestInternal(snapshot.policy);
                string canonicalJson = SerializeCanonicalJson(manifest, canonicalNormalize: true);

                string fingerprint;
                using (var sha = SHA256.Create())
                {
                    byte[] jsonBytes = Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(canonicalJson);
                    fingerprint = BitConverter.ToString(sha.ComputeHash(jsonBytes)).Replace("-", "").ToUpperInvariant();
                }

                if (!_globalCache.TryPublishComputedEntry(
                    snapshot.generation,
                    snapshot.policy,
                    manifest,
                    canonicalJson,
                    fingerprint,
                    out string? rejectionReason,
                    out CoherentContentProfileCacheEntry? publishedEntry))
                {
                    string errMsg = $"Computed content profile entry could not be published or validated against current state stamp: {rejectionReason}";
                    Log.Error($"[ContentProfileProvider] {errMsg}");
                    throw new InvalidOperationException(errMsg);
                }

                return new ComputedContentProfileResult(manifest, canonicalJson, fingerprint, publishedEntry!);
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                if (capturedGen >= 0)
                {
                    _globalCache.SetComputationError(capturedGen, ex.ToString());
                }
                else
                {
                    _globalCache.SetComputationError(ex.ToString());
                }
                Log.Error($"[ContentProfileProvider] Failed to compute ContentProfile: {ex}");
                throw;
            }
        }

        public static string ComputeActualContentProfileFingerprint()
        {
            return ComputeAndPublishActualContentProfile().Fingerprint;
        }

        public bool TryPublishComputedEntry(
            long expectedGeneration,
            ExpectedPackagePolicyRecord? capturedPolicy,
            ContentProfileManifest manifest,
            string canonicalJson,
            string fingerprint,
            out string? rejectionReason,
            out CoherentContentProfileCacheEntry? publishedEntry)
        {
            if (manifest == null) throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(manifest));
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(canonicalJson)) throw new ArgumentException("canonicalJson cannot be null or empty", nameof(canonicalJson));
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(fingerprint)) throw new ArgumentException("fingerprint cannot be null or empty", nameof(fingerprint));

            lock (_sync)
            {
                if (_generation != expectedGeneration)
                {
                    rejectionReason = $"Stale configuration generation: captured was {expectedGeneration}, but current is {_generation}.";
                    publishedEntry = null;
                    return false;
                }

                if (_configuredPolicy == null)
                {
                    rejectionReason = "No configured package policy present in cache state.";
                    publishedEntry = null;
                    return false;
                }

                string currentDigest = _configuredPolicy.policyDigest ?? "";
                string capturedDigest = capturedPolicy?.policyDigest ?? "";
                if (!string.Equals(currentDigest, capturedDigest, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                {
                    rejectionReason = $"Policy digest mismatch: captured was '{capturedDigest}', but current is '{currentDigest}'.";
                    publishedEntry = null;
                    return false;
                }

                string policyId = _configuredPolicy?.policyId ?? "";
                string policyRevision = _configuredPolicy?.revision ?? "";

                _entry = new CoherentContentProfileCacheEntry(
                    _generation,
                    currentDigest,
                    policyId,
                    policyRevision,
                    fingerprint,
                    canonicalJson,
                    manifest,
                    manifest.contentContractVersion ?? ContentProfileProvider.CONTENT_CONTRACT_VERSION,
                    DateTime.UtcNow);

                _lastError = null;
                rejectionReason = null;
                publishedEntry = _entry;
                return true;
            }
        }

        public bool TryGetCoherentEntry(out CoherentContentProfileCacheEntry? entry)
        {
            lock (_sync)
            {
                if (_entry != null && _entry.ConfigurationGeneration == _generation)
                {
                    entry = _entry;
                    return true;
                }
                entry = null;
                return false;
            }
        }

        private sealed class ComputedContentProfileResult
        {
            public ContentProfileManifest Manifest { get; }
            public string CanonicalJson { get; }
            public string Fingerprint { get; }
            public CoherentContentProfileCacheEntry PublishedEntry { get; }

            public ComputedContentProfileResult(
                ContentProfileManifest manifest,
                string canonicalJson,
                string fingerprint,
                CoherentContentProfileCacheEntry publishedEntry)
            {
                Manifest = manifest ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(manifest));
                CanonicalJson = canonicalJson ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(canonicalJson));
                Fingerprint = fingerprint ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(fingerprint));
                PublishedEntry = publishedEntry ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(publishedEntry));
            }
        }

        private static ComputedContentProfileResult ComputeAndPublishActualContentProfile()
        {
            long capturedGen = -1;
            try
            {
                _globalCache.ClearComputationError();
                var snapshot = _globalCache.CaptureStateSnapshot();
                capturedGen = snapshot.generation;
                if (snapshot.policy == null)
                {
                    throw new InvalidOperationException("ContentProfile computation requires an explicit expected package policy to be configured before trusted actual content profile success. Status: UNCONFIGURED (BLOCKED_NO_POLICY).");
                }

                var manifest = CollectActualContentProfileManifestInternal(snapshot.policy);
                string canonicalJson = SerializeCanonicalJson(manifest, canonicalNormalize: true);

                string fingerprint;
                using (var sha = SHA256.Create())
                {
                    byte[] jsonBytes = Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(canonicalJson);
                    fingerprint = BitConverter.ToString(sha.ComputeHash(jsonBytes)).Replace("-", "").ToUpperInvariant();
                }

                if (!_globalCache.TryPublishComputedEntry(
                    snapshot.generation,
                    snapshot.policy,
                    manifest,
                    canonicalJson,
                    fingerprint,
                    out string? rejectionReason,
                    out CoherentContentProfileCacheEntry? publishedEntry))
                {
                    string errMsg = $"Computed content profile entry could not be published or validated against current state stamp: {rejectionReason}";
                    Log.Error($"[ContentProfileProvider] {errMsg}");
                    throw new InvalidOperationException(errMsg);
                }

                return new ComputedContentProfileResult(manifest, canonicalJson, fingerprint, publishedEntry!);
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                if (capturedGen >= 0)
                {
                    _globalCache.SetComputationError(capturedGen, ex.ToString());
                }
                else
                {
                    _globalCache.SetComputationError(ex.ToString());
                }
                Log.Error($"[ContentProfileProvider] Failed to compute ContentProfile: {ex}");
                throw;
            }
        }

        public static ContentProfileManifest ComputeActualContentProfileManifest()
        {
            return ComputeAndPublishActualContentProfile().Manifest;
        }

        public static string ComputeActualContentProfileFingerprint()
        {
            return ComputeAndPublishActualContentProfile().Fingerprint;

**Status:** PROPOSED (Not Accepted)
**Decision Owner:** Master (GPT-5.6 Sol)
**Project:** WarEconomy / RimMulti

## 1. Context & Baseline
This ADR defines the configuration and content manifest contracts necessary to prevent client/Worker content drift, silent semantic load loss, and the weaponization of "fail-closed" mechanics. It operates within the upstream constraints established in ACCEPTED ADR-001 (Version/Protocol Admission)[cite: 16], ADR-003 (Hostile Checkpoint Validation)[cite: 18], ADR-006A (Temporal Schema Classification)[cite: 17], ADR-007 (Writer Lease Admission)[cite: 19], and ADR-008 (World-Layer Content)[cite: 23].

## 2. Profile Identity Model
To enforce strict content parity, the Dedicated Server utilizes a distinct profile identity and revision model:
*   **`ContentProfileId`:** A stable identifier for the lineage or name of the server's approved content profile.
*   **`ContentProfileFingerprint`:** The immutable, exact gameplay profile identity. It is a deterministic hash or strict signature of the RimWorld build/revision, official DLC set, approved mod package IDs, mod versions/hashes, deterministic load order, and approved gameplay-content capability set.
*   **`ContentProfileRevision`:** The monotonic world-level sequence of accepted profile migrations/adoptions.

All artifacts, checkpoints, client sessions, and Worker materializations must securely bind to the exact `ContentProfileFingerprint` they were produced under.

## 3. Schema & Codec Binding
Artifact and checkpoint metadata must be strictly bound to their generation context to decide between compatible loads, migration requirements, or outright rejection[cite: 18]. The metadata must include:
*   The exact `ContentProfileFingerprint` and `ContentProfileId`.
*   The `ContentProfileRevision`.
*   The **Serialization/Schema Version** of the state format.
*   The **Temporal/Semantic Codec Version** (specifically where ADR-006A typed temporal fields depend on it for interpretation)[cite: 17].

## 4. Admission Contracts & ADR-001 Alignment
Content and profile compatibility checks are admission and handshake gates; they do *not* constitute authentication[cite: 16].
*   **Handshake Pipeline:** The architecture strictly preserves the ADR-001 lifecycle: `CONNECTED` $\rightarrow$ `HANDSHAKE_PENDING` $\rightarrow$ `AUTHENTICATED` $\rightarrow$ `WORLD_READY`[cite: 16]. Protocol and mod compatibility checks occur during `HANDSHAKE_PENDING`[cite: 16].
*   **Checkpoint & Artifact Validation:** Owner checkpoints entering canonical validation (ADR-003) must match the expected `ContentProfileFingerprint`[cite: 18].
*   **Engine Materialization:** Ordinary clients, Tactical Workers, and Shared World pathing executors must initialize using the exact pinned profile[cite: 19, 23]. No gameplay mutation may proceed if the required gameplay content profile is incompatible[cite: 16].

## 5. Dependency Closure Policy
Static proof alone is an insufficient acceptance oracle for RimWorld modifications due to dynamic code and generated references. Dependency closure is enforced via layered approval:
1.  **Manifest/Hash/Load-Order Validation:** Standard byte and version parity checks.
2.  **Typed Static Registry/Reference Validation:** Preflight checks for known, statically analyzable references (e.g., XML cross-references) where possible[cite: 18].
3.  **Server-Controlled Engine Semantic Load:** Loading the profile into a controlled, headless engine to evaluate deep load semantics[cite: 18].
4.  **Post-Load Graph/Reference/Identity Checks:** Validating identity, counts, and component attachments post-initialization.
5.  **Explicit Disposition:** Any unclassified, unsupported, or ambiguous content discovered during validation receives an explicit rejection or quarantine disposition.

## 6. Runtime Failure Invariant
A pinned approved profile guarantees that untrusted participants cannot introduce content drift into a lawful Tactical or ordinary session. However, it cannot make all runtime content/schema failures impossible.
*   **Defect Handling:** Runtime operator/server defects or corrupted canonical state trigger a `QUARANTINED` or `REPAIR_REQUIRED` status[cite: 17, 18].
*   **No Silent Drop:** Failures must never silently delete data, drop entities, or ignore unresolvable references[cite: 18].
*   **No Defender Immunity:** "Fail-closed" mechanics must never be interpreted or exploitable as a defender-controlled immunity mechanism against lawful offline attacks (FR-153)[cite: 14].

## 7. Configuration Authority & Retroactivity
The Dedicated Server is authoritative over all gameplay configurations. Ambiguity regarding whether a configuration change affects past events is resolved by categorizing all `ConfigRevision` fields into explicit retroactivity policies:
*   **`IMMEDIATELY_PROSPECTIVE`:** Applies instantly to all new calculations (e.g., global NPC market recovery rates)[cite: 14].
*   **`OPERATION_SNAPSHOTTED`:** The config value applies to a specific operation and must not retroactively change. The durable operation state *must* record the effective config value or immutable config snapshot reference used when the operation was created[cite: 16]. Later replay/recovery must use this snapshotted value, never the current config[cite: 16].
*   **`SESSION_OR_RESTART_BOUND`:** Requires a server restart or a new player session to apply (e.g., map generation constraints)[cite: 14].
*   **`MIGRATION_REQUIRED`:** A config schema change that is severe enough to require a formal world migration sequence.
*   **`NON_RETROACTIVE_HISTORICAL`:** Values that purely document past states and cannot alter durably committed operations.

## 8. Content Migration Pipeline & States
When the `ContentProfileRevision` advances, older canonical artifacts cannot safely load directly under the new profile unless the migration mechanism explicitly supports a dual-profile adapter.
*   **Conceptual Flow:** Old-profile compatible read/materialization $\rightarrow$ Migration Transform $\rightarrow$ New-profile semantic validation $\rightarrow$ New canonical artifact adoption. (Exact transaction/rollback mechanics remain ADR-004 scope).
*   **Migration State Machine:**
    *   `CURRENT`: The world is running normally on the active profile.
    *   `MIGRATION_REQUIRED`: A new profile is staged, and the world is halted awaiting transformation.
    *   `MIGRATION_PENDING`: Migration operations are queued.
    *   `MIGRATING`: The server-controlled migration engine is processing the artifact graph.
    *   `QUARANTINED`: Migration failed (e.g., unresolvable semantic loss). Operator intervention required.
    *   `CURRENT (new)`: The world successfully adopted the new `ContentProfileRevision`.

*(Note: `REPAIR_REQUIRED` is kept strictly for defective/corrupted canonical state, not planned version migrations)[cite: 16, 17].*

## 9. Cosmetic Capability Model
Client-only cosmetic mods may bypass strict gameplay-content parity only if they conform to a server-approved **Cosmetic Capability Profile**.
*   The profile defines known, allowed hooks and resources.
*   The mod must possess no serialized gameplay state.
*   The mod must perform no simulation Def mutation.
*   The mod must not provide authority-sensitive input bypasses.
*   **Admission:** If a client mod exceeds the approved cosmetic capability profile, admission fails closed and the client is rejected at the handshake[cite: 16].

Decision:
Do not revert the fresh-process validator architecture.

Gate04 established that a fresh RimWorld process can load exact staged bytes and compare supported semantic state.

Gate05 must fix the provenance/control path:
- who creates the validation task;
- where the expected sealed result comes from;
- how the simulator knows the validator result belongs to that exact task/result/stage.

## MD-126 — Validator Task Is Simulator/Operator-Owned, Not Caller-Nominated

Decision:
The simulator/operator creates an immutable `ValidatorTask` from its own current sealed result.

A caller may request validation to run, but may not supply:
- expected manifest JSON/hash;
- SealedResultId/epoch authority;
- arbitrary receipt;
- arbitrary validator identity.

Preferred Gate05 PoC shape:
1. simulator has immutable current SealedResult;
2. simulator creates random ValidatorTaskId/capability bound to exact stage/result/context;
3. simulator/operator launches a fresh validator process;
4. expected result is supplied from the task generated by the simulator, not from a caller field;
5. validator loads exact staged SHA and computes actual manifest;
6. validator returns task-bound result over an operator-controlled channel/capability;
7. simulator creates/accepts StageValidationReceipt only for that exact task.

Public-key cryptography is not required.
A process-owned local pipe + unguessable task capability/nonce or equivalent operator-controlled mechanism is sufficient for the PoC threat model.

## MD-127 — Public Caller-Submitted Receipt Is Not Promotion Authority

Decision:
`SUBMIT_STAGE_VALIDATION_RECEIPT <caller JSON>` must not be a generic public authority transition.

Promotion authority must originate from an internally registered validator task/result.

If a compatibility/debug submit command remains, it cannot transition the canonical simulator into STAGED_VALIDATED unless the receipt can be matched to an outstanding operator-owned validator task and its protected result channel/capability.

PID inequality is diagnostic only, never issuer proof.

## MD-128 — Complete Result/Receipt Context Is Closed-Schema Equality

Decision:
Stage validation and promotion must bind and compare every authority-defining field in the supported contract, including:
- ValidatorTaskId/capability;
- staged path + staged SHA;
- source artifact hash;
- AuthorityId;
- StoreIncarnation/baseLineage placeholder;
- GrantId;
- WorkerGeneration;
- scopeId;
- stable target context/map identity;
- allowed operation mode;
- ContentProfileFingerprint;
- SupportedSemanticManifest version;
- SealedResultId;
- ResultEpoch/currentResultEpoch;
- sealed manifest hash;
- actual validator-computed manifest hash.

No "carried but unchecked" authority field is allowed.

## MD-129 — Control-Plane Validation Failures Revoke Stale Capabilities

Decision:
For authority/grant/profile/input/validator-task/receipt validation commands, any malformed or semantically invalid attempt clears stale execution/promotion capabilities according to the state machine:
- trustedSimulationReady false;
- active seal/stage receipt invalid where relevant;
- STEP/SEAL/STAGE/PROMOTE blocked until explicit clean reset/re-admission.

Ordinary read/query syntax errors need not revoke unrelated authority; this decision applies to control-plane authority transitions.

## MD-130 — ContentProfile Uses an Actual Loaded-Content Manifest

Decision:
ModsConfig XML hash alone is not the accepted ADR-006B ContentProfileFingerprint.

Gate05 PoC must construct a canonical content manifest from actual admitted content sufficient to detect authority-relevant drift.

At minimum include/bind:
- RimWorld build/version and relevant core assembly identity;
- active mod package IDs/order;
- admitted mod assembly SHA/MVID inventory;
- DLC/mod version/content identity available to the runtime;
- canonical Def/content census or another ADR-006B-compatible semantic content digest;
- profile schema/version/capabilities.

Expected profile is operator-approved; Worker and validator independently compute/verify actual loaded profile before trusted admission/validation.

## MD-131 — Unsafe Replacement Fallback Is Fail-Closed

Decision:
For an existing approved final, if the verified same-volume atomic replacement primitive cannot be used, promotion fails closed and preserves the prior final.

Do not fall back to copy-overwrite/delete for canonical promotion.

A first-time final with no prior file may use a separately validated same-volume atomic rename/move path.

## MD-132 — Gate04 Semantic Scope Is Corrected to Actual V4 Evidence

Decision:
Current V4 supported manifest evidence includes:
- active JobDef;
- active job loadID;
- targetA/B/C representations implemented by the census;
- reservation claimant/job/target/maxPawns/stackCount;
plus the other declared V4 fields independently exercised.
